message.content:
{
  "moments": [
    {
      "local_key": "m1_automated_inquiry_path",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0161"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0147",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0174",
      "quote": "we've still closed these weddings that have come from these leads just through our automated processes.",
      "context_summary": "Marisa compared 17 DJ Hybrid events completed in 2025 with an expectation of 90 by the end of “this year,” and described a large increase in activity. She said the lead-to-first-call path was self-service and that the team had closed weddings from those leads without much outside outreach or follow-up. Whitney checked where manual work begins, and Marisa confirmed the system was handling the path through the first call.",
      "moment_type": "result",
      "proposition": "Marisa reported that DJ Hybrid’s automated lead process was supporting a higher volume of events and wedding bookings with limited manual outreach, while the 90-event figure was a year-end expectation, not a completed result.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners managing growth may care whether their inquiry process can handle more demand without requiring constant manual follow-up, and which parts of the journey still need their attention.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The event counts and booking description are client-reported, not independently verified.",
        "The 90-event figure was expected by year-end, not reported as achieved.",
        "The exchange does not establish that advertising alone caused the increase or that all bookings were ad-attributed."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 5,
      "reasons": [
        "The exchange includes a client-reported business change and a clarification of what the automation does.",
        "Whitney checks task ownership rather than treating the process as entirely automated."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["service_value", "audience_insight", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Whitney asks where manual work begins and confirms the distinction between automated lead handling and the team's calls.",
        "attention_reason": "The conversation connects reported business activity to a concrete inquiry-process boundary, while leaving attribution and causation open.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m1_sales_and_attribution",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0225"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0186",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0245",
      "quote": "my brain doesn't even think like that.",
      "context_summary": "Marisa wanted to compare Funktastic and DJ Hybrid despite their different price points. Whitney cited one May Google Ads lead reportedly turning into a $14,000 Funktastic booking and proposed adding sales figures to future reports and looking back at earlier months. Mike said that kind of comparison was useful to him. Whitney distinguished ad-attributed inquiries from broader business growth and described how a person might encounter an ad but inquire later through another channel. Mike noted that some planners contact him directly and are not in LeadLock; Marisa added that callers often say they saw DJ Hybrid on Instagram, which she inferred may have been an ad.",
      "moment_type": "observation",
      "proposition": "The exchange shows WIA and the clients trying to interpret sales alongside ad-attributed inquiries: the client valued help translating a reported booking into an advertising comparison, while both sides recognized that platform attribution may miss part of a buyer's journey.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners may have sales, referrals, direct planner contacts, and ad-attributed inquiries that do not appear in one reporting view; interpreting each without conflating them can affect how they judge advertising.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The one May booking and its Google Ads attribution are reported in the conversation, not independently verified.",
        "Whitney's comparison to year-to-date ad spend is not accompanied by an itemized cost basis in this exchange; no ROI multiple is asserted here.",
        "Mike's approximately 30% year-to-date business growth was attributed to what his accountant and bookkeeper said, not to advertising.",
        "Marisa's Instagram observation is anecdotal, and her belief that the exposure was an ad is not confirmed."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 5,
      "reasons": [
        "The exchange preserves a client question about how to understand advertising value, not just a platform metric.",
        "WIA distinguishes direct attribution from possible broader influence, and the clients add concrete gaps in tracking."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "wia_expertise", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Whitney proposes including sales figures in reports, requests historical figures, and explains why attributed inquiries and overall business trends should be viewed separately.",
        "attention_reason": "The interaction makes the limits of attribution tangible while showing the client's need for help interpreting sales data; its reported figures require careful boundaries.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m1_brand_alignment",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0129"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0115",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0134",
      "quote": "we'll want everything to feel cohesive, you know?",
      "context_summary": "Marisa said the branding was done and the website was being built, with some copy still under edit. Whitney suggested getting approved logos, fonts, colors, and any brand guide so WIA could begin refreshing the ads traffic landing pages while the new site was in progress. Marisa agreed and said she would check what assets and guide were available.",
      "moment_type": "decision",
      "proposition": "Whitney recommended coordinating the client’s in-progress rebrand with the ad-traffic landing pages rather than waiting for the new website to be finished; Marisa agreed to check and share the brand assets.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners changing their brand may need the experience after an ad click to keep pace with the new identity, while coordinating work across separate website and advertising projects.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The assets had not yet been confirmed as shared, and the landing-page refresh was proposed, not reported as completed.",
        "The exchange does not establish a performance result from brand alignment."
      ],
      "claim_status": "planned",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "The recommendation connects a client-owned rebrand to the landing-page experience.",
        "The client supplies the status of the rebrand and agrees to check the materials, making the collaboration visible."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["wia_expertise", "service_value", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Whitney identifies which brand materials would let WIA start aligning ad-traffic landing pages with the new website.",
        "attention_reason": "This is a concrete example of coordinating work across a client's site and WIA's advertising touchpoints, with implementation still pending.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m1_product_value_distinction",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0270"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0260",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0273",
      "quote": "harder to, like, articulate the value, because it's a wedding band",
      "context_summary": "Marisa proposed a walkthrough of the rebrand so the team could better understand how the two products were differentiated. She said Funktastic’s wedding-band value was harder for her to articulate than DJ Hybrid’s newer, more immediately visible saxophone offering. Whitney’s responses in this short exchange do not develop or resolve the positioning question.",
      "moment_type": "tension",
      "proposition": "Marisa identified an internal positioning challenge: one product’s value was harder for her to explain than the newer product’s conspicuous feature, and she suggested a rebrand walkthrough to help the team understand the distinction.",
      "audience_relevance": "Businesses with multiple offers may find that a visible novelty is easier to communicate than the value of a more established or less immediately demonstrable service.",
      "qualifications": [
        "This is Marisa's assessment; the exchange does not establish how couples describe or compare the products.",
        "The rebrand walkthrough and any resulting messaging changes are not reported as completed."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 3,
      "reasons": [
        "The client identifies a specific value-articulation problem rather than a generic request for more advertising.",
        "The buyer-facing distinction and any resolution remain unknown, so the exchange supports a research question rather than a finished conclusion."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "research_needed",
        "wia_contribution": null,
        "attention_reason": "This could reveal how businesses communicate the value of related offers, but the source has the client's diagnosis without buyer evidence or a developed team response.",
        "research_questions": [
          "What specific buyer language or product attributes distinguish Funktastic from DJ Hybrid, and did the rebrand walkthrough change how the client or team explained that difference?"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m1_market_research_and_client_knowledge",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0360"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0359",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0426",
      "quote": "And usually the response that I get is, like, we have great reviews, like, check out our reviews, right?",
      "context_summary": "Whitney distinguished reviews from asking new clients why they chose a business, then proposed short post-contract market-research surveys for both brands, with responses visible to the clients and WIA. Marisa and Mike added that buyer responses could reveal which features attract couples and that knowing personal details could help musicians feel connected to the couple. Marisa asked whether those questions belonged in an operational wedding form. Whitney recommended keeping the research survey separate from the pre-wedding planning form, described sending the research survey shortly after signing while the decision was fresh, and explained a possible division of information between WIA and the client. Marisa said the survey link could fit into the existing welcome flow; Whitney planned to draft questions for client review before building the surveys.",
      "moment_type": "mechanism",
      "proposition": "Whitney proposed gathering fresh post-purchase reasons for choosing each brand, distinct from reviews and operational planning questions; the clients added that the answers could inform both marketing differentiation and the musicians' understanding of the couple.",
      "audience_relevance": "Wedding businesses may already have reviews and client forms but still lack a dedicated way to learn what influenced a choice while that decision is recent.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The survey questions and automations were proposed for client review; the exchange does not establish that surveys were built, sent, or answered.",
        "The clients' examples are possible topics and uses, not confirmed buyer preferences or results."
      ],
      "claim_status": "planned",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 5,
      "reasons": [
        "The team distinguishes reputation material from direct evidence about why buyers chose a business.",
        "Client knowledge changes the proposed survey's purpose and reveals a separate operational need.",
        "The exchange includes timing, question format, data visibility, client review, and a practical way to fit the survey into an existing welcome flow."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "wia_expertise", "service_value", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Whitney explains the distinction between reviews and market research, proposes survey timing and structure, separates buyer research from wedding-day operations, and offers a draft-review-build sequence.",
        "attention_reason": "This is a detailed collaboration in which WIA's research proposal is shaped by the clients' knowledge of their buyers and service operations.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m1_creative_refresh_judgment",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m1.t0279"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m1.t0274",
      "context_last_span_id": "m1.t0282",
      "quote": "if something's working, I normally don't try to change it a lot, because that can actually affect the algorithm.",
      "context_summary": "Marisa asked how often ads were refreshed. Carmen said new creatives were available each month, noted she needed to do better at sending the client new content for an approved-content bank, and described avoiding major changes when something was working. She said retargeting was typically refreshed less often, while the Funktastic conversion campaign had been refreshed after performance declined and was relaunched that day. She described refresh decisions as performance-dependent rather than strictly month-to-month.",
      "moment_type": "mechanism",
      "proposition": "Carmen described a performance-led approach to creative changes: make new assets available, avoid unnecessary changes to working ads, and refresh campaigns when performance signals warrant it.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners may want to know what happens to new content they provide and why an agency would not replace every working ad on a fixed schedule.",
      "qualifications": [
        "Carmen's statement about algorithm effects is her rationale; this exchange supplies no test or measured result establishing the effect.",
        "The Funktastic campaign had just been relaunched, so its subsequent performance was not yet known."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "The client asks about the working cadence, and Carmen explains how performance, approved assets, and campaign type affect decisions.",
        "The exchange distinguishes having fresh creative available from changing every active ad on a fixed calendar."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["wia_expertise", "service_value", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Carmen explains the reported refresh approach and acknowledges the need to send the client's new content more consistently for approval and use.",
        "attention_reason": "The exchange makes routine campaign management decisions visible and preserves that the relaunch had no reported outcome yet.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m2_low_search_volume_and_testing",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m2.t0083"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m2.t0051",
      "context_last_span_id": "m2.t0098",
      "quote": "I think the only issue keeping a campaign on is if it's getting clicks and then not getting leads, because then it's just a waste of money.",
      "context_summary": "Bri asked about the senior-photo campaign after saying reports were difficult for her to interpret without an explanation. Carmen described very low search volume in the 30A area, said broadening the terms was still producing impressions but no clicks, and asked Bri when she normally received inquiries. Bri said senior inquiries were generally stable but infrequent, under ten a month. Carmen suggested that visual Meta advertising might suit the audience, but said leaving the current search campaign on was not costing money without clicks and could allow a seasonal increase to become visible. Whitney guessed that back-to-school might bring more traction. Carmen named clicks without leads as a reason to reconsider; Bri agreed that it remained a test.",
      "moment_type": "decision",
      "proposition": "The team and client treated low activity as a question of limited local demand and possible timing, not simply as proof of a failed campaign: Bri supplied her inquiry pattern, and Carmen recommended watching for a change in engagement before deciding whether to keep the campaign.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners in small markets or with infrequently purchased services may need to distinguish low search demand from a campaign that attracts clicks but fails to generate inquiries.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The search-volume, impression, and inquiry figures are reported in the conversation, not independently verified.",
        "Seasonality and the back-to-school hypothesis were unresolved; no later campaign result is supplied.",
        "The possible Meta approach was a suggestion, not a reported launch."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 5,
      "reasons": [
        "Carmen asks for client knowledge about inquiry timing before settling on a technical explanation.",
        "The exchange includes a conditional keep-or-reconsider rationale rather than an unconditional recommendation.",
        "The client is invited to interpret performance in context, after saying the report alone was hard to understand."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "wia_expertise", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Carmen explains the low-volume and no-click situation, asks Bri about real inquiry timing, and identifies clicks without leads as a point for reconsideration; Whitney offers a seasonal hypothesis.",
        "attention_reason": "The decision depends on local search limits, the client's experience, and what future engagement looks like, with no result yet to confirm the seasonal hypothesis.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m2_transition_from_full_service",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m2.t0106"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m2.t0102",
      "context_last_span_id": "m2.t0131",
      "quote": "Yeah, I feel like another month, like July could be the last month is what I'm thinking.",
      "context_summary": "Whitney checked whether Bri was ready to move from full-service ads management to taking responsibility for the ads with consultative support, or wanted another month. Bri said July could be the last month of full service. Whitney proposed a follow-up around the next billing cycle to confirm the timing and discuss possible monthly or quarterly consulting calls. Bri agreed to that plan, and they scheduled a July meeting.",
      "moment_type": "decision",
      "proposition": "The client expressed a tentative timeline for ending full-service management, and Whitney responded by setting a check-in to confirm readiness and discuss a more consultative arrangement rather than assuming the transition was immediate.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners considering a change in support may want room to make the decision around their capacity and billing cycle, with a way to discuss what support could remain.",
      "qualifications": [
        "Bri said July could be the last month; the final transition was not confirmed in this exchange.",
        "The consultative cadence was discussed as a possible next step, not established here as a current offer or completed service."
      ],
      "claim_status": "planned",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "The client sets the proposed timing, and Whitney asks about readiness rather than imposing a transition date.",
        "The discussion identifies a specific decision point and a possible continuity-of-support conversation."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "service_value"],
        "destination": "public_opportunity",
        "wia_contribution": "Whitney checks the client's timing, proposes a follow-up aligned with the billing cycle, and describes possible consultative support for discussion.",
        "attention_reason": "This interaction shows a service transition being paced with the client's readiness, while the exact next arrangement remains undecided.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m3_agency_scope_and_workload",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m3.t0070"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m3.t0064",
      "context_last_span_id": "m3.t0119",
      "quote": "I've worked with agencies where the retainer that they're charging clients is like 5,000 to $5,500 a month",
      "context_summary": "Carmen described a difficult client relationship and asked Fallon about agency experiences. Fallon said that in prior agency roles some clients paid retainers of about $5,000–$5,500 a month and spent at least $5,000 a month on Meta. She attributed those arrangements to a larger workload, including more creative output, custom copy and funnel work, and more frequent reporting. She also described how higher spending and client expectations could increase pressure on teams, and said she had experienced burnout. Carmen asked whether the retainer reflected service quality or customer service and later compared the workload with her current experience.",
      "moment_type": "observation",
      "proposition": "Fallon described higher-spend agency arrangements as involving more work and output, not just a higher fee, while also describing potential pressure and burnout; Carmen elicited the distinction through follow-up questions.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners assessing agency fees may care what work, output, reporting cadence, and team demands are included, while service providers may need to consider the operational cost of scope.",
      "qualifications": [
        "These are Fallon's recollections of prior agency roles, including work with coaches and digital-product businesses as well as other industries; they are not a wedding-industry benchmark.",
        "The retainer and media-spend figures are reported examples, not verified market rates or current WIA pricing.",
        "Fallon's comments about burnout are her experience and are not a claim about all agencies or clients."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "internal_only",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "The discussion connects price to the actual scope and volume of work rather than treating the fee in isolation.",
        "It is useful internal audience and service-scope intelligence, but the examples do not support a public industry benchmark."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["audience_insight", "service_value", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "internal_intelligence",
        "wia_contribution": "Carmen asks what might explain the higher retainers and workload, prompting Fallon to distinguish customer service, team structure, creative output, and reporting cadence.",
        "attention_reason": "The exchange offers firsthand, bounded intelligence about how clients may experience agency cost and control, alongside the operational pressures behind scope.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m3_lead_lull_diagnosis",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m3.t0214"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m3.t0200",
      "context_last_span_id": "m3.t0250",
      "quote": "Are you seeing that organically too? Or like, is it just on the paid side?",
      "context_summary": "Fallon asked whether Davis and Gray's reported lead slowdown was happening organically as well as through Google Ads. She said she checked LeadLock and saw a lull across both sources, then discussed the client's wish to focus on more specific locations. Fallon reported that the client updated the landing page and Fallon changed Google targeting; she recalled a short period with about four leads in a week, followed by another lull, and said Meta had only recently gone live so there was not enough data. Fallon was unsure whether the pattern was historical or pointed to the ads or page, and planned to look further back. Carmen said she lacked enough historical account context to answer confidently after covering other work.",
      "moment_type": "tension",
      "proposition": "Fallon checked whether a lead slowdown was limited to paid traffic, found a reported lull across organic and paid sources, and described changes followed by a brief increase and another lull; she and Carmen left the cause unresolved and identified further historical review as a next step.",
      "audience_relevance": "When inquiries decline, owners may need to distinguish a channel-specific issue from a broader slowdown and examine both lead patterns and the experience before an inquiry is submitted.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The figures and sequence are Fallon's reported account history; the exchange does not independently verify them.",
        "The remembered increase of about four leads in a week followed both targeting and client-made landing-page changes, so the source does not establish which change, if any, caused it.",
        "Meta had only recently launched, and the cause of the later lull remained unknown."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "internal_only",
      "strength": 5,
      "reasons": [
        "Fallon's diagnostic question changes the inquiry from a paid-only issue to a cross-channel investigation.",
        "The team preserves uncertainty about cause and does not present the temporary increase as a sustained result.",
        "Carmen explicitly states the limit of her historical context."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["wia_expertise", "audience_insight", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "internal_intelligence",
        "wia_contribution": "Fallon compares paid and organic lead patterns, reviews the client record, and identifies historical review as a next step; Carmen is transparent that she cannot supply a reliable historical comparison.",
        "attention_reason": "This is a useful diagnostic exchange because the lead slowdown spans channels, the brief recovery did not last, and the team does not claim a cause it cannot establish.",
        "research_questions": []
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m3_tag_verification_issue",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m3.t0355"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m3.t0325",
      "context_last_span_id": "m3.t0373",
      "quote": "I have to make sure that they have a Google tag. Otherwise, honestly, like, they're just kind of wasting money on Google Ads.",
      "context_summary": "Carmen brought Fallon into a live Google Tag Manager check for an account discussed as Diamond Day Ranch. Carmen said a test showed the tag was present but previewing a page view did not connect. She checked LeadLock and reviewed earlier call recordings to confirm how the tag had been added to the client's WordPress site, including the header and footer. Fallon said she had also seen Google errors recently and described adding GTM on a Wix site as straightforward. They did not resolve whether the preview failure meant the tag was absent or whether the verification tool was malfunctioning.",
      "moment_type": "observation",
      "proposition": "Carmen investigated a mismatch between a tag appearing to be installed and a preview that failed to connect, checking the site's setup and prior implementation records; the reason for the mismatch remained unresolved.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners spending on search ads need trustworthy conversion measurement, while technical checks can produce conflicting signals that require verification before drawing conclusions about tracking.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The source does not establish whether the tag was absent, incorrectly installed, or affected by a preview-tool issue.",
        "Carmen's concern about wasted spend is not evidence that tracking or advertising had actually failed.",
        "No final installation test or subsequent outcome is reported."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "internal_only",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "The exchange shows hands-on troubleshooting across the tag manager, site, and prior implementation record.",
        "The technical discrepancy and its business significance are visible, but the resolution is not."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["wia_expertise", "service_value"],
        "destination": "research_needed",
        "wia_contribution": "Carmen tests the tag, checks LeadLock and the WordPress setup, and consults earlier call recordings; Fallon contributes a comparison with a recent Wix installation and similar Google errors.",
        "attention_reason": "The case could demonstrate how WIA investigates a measurement problem, but it cannot support a claim about the tag's status or the cause of the failed preview yet.",
        "research_questions": [
          "Was the Google tag ultimately verified on the account's current site, and what explained the mismatch between the installation check and the failed preview?"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m4_campaign_comparison_reconciliation",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m4.t0170"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m4.t0089",
      "context_last_span_id": "m4.t0179",
      "quote": "I still do think, though, that this Maximize Clicks campaign is a lot better.",
      "context_summary": "Carmen had Jillian inspect Change History to establish when the campaign changed back to Maximize Clicks, then compared the earlier and later date ranges. They discussed platform costs per conversion and booked-appointment counts, but the displayed totals and date ranges did not align cleanly during the screen review. Jillian added that some appointments were repeats and that one person cancelled after missing the location; her description of how many were new was not fully consistent in the exchange. Carmen described booking costs on individual days and viewed the campaign as trending in the right direction, though the overall difference was modest. Jillian agreed the switch back seemed like a good choice and said appointment volume had historically arrived in spikes.",
      "moment_type": "tension",
      "proposition": "Carmen used Change History and date-range comparisons to assess a campaign change, while Jillian supplied booking context that made platform conversion counts harder to interpret; both saw possible improvement, but the exchange did not establish a clean before-and-after result.",
      "audience_relevance": "Owners evaluating a campaign change may need to reconcile platform conversions with actual appointment quality, repeats, cancellations, and the correct comparison period.",
      "qualifications": [
        "The reported dashboard figures and booking counts were not fully reconciled in this review.",
        "Jillian's description of new, repeat, and cancelled appointments is unclear in the transcript.",
        "The comparison does not establish a measured causal effect of the campaign change, and the reported outcome is not independently verified."
      ],
      "claim_status": "reported",
      "sensitivity": "unknown",
      "strength": 4,
      "reasons": [
        "Carmen checks the change history rather than comparing performance without first locating the change.",
        "The client's appointment context exposes a gap between platform conversions and business outcomes.",
        "The team's tentative conclusion is preserved alongside the unresolved figures."
      ],
      "discovery": {
        "lenses": ["wia_expertise", "audience_insight", "broader_principle"],
        "destination": "research_needed",
        "wia_contribution": "Carmen guides the date-range comparison, checks Change History, explains cost-per-appointment figures, and makes a tentative assessment rather than presenting the comparison as conclusive.",
        "attention_reason": "The exchange is a useful example of live campaign review, but the conflicting counts and periods make a stronger performance claim premature.",
        "research_questions": [
          "For the intended before-and-after dates, what were the final platform conversion totals and the reconciled number of unique, new booked appointments after repeats and cancellations?"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "m4_local_video_campaign_question",
      "anchor_span_ids": ["m4.t0195"],
      "context_first_span_id": "m4.t0184",
      "context_last_span_id": "m4.t0211",
      "quote": "Yeah, it's in the area that we target.",
